summary: The dedicated country dossier examined Goa specifically: the territory retains a Portuguese-derived civil-code tradition and is India's main foreign-tourism destination, but no divergent trans statute or enforcement pattern was found, and Goa is not among the 12 states/UTs that have constituted the mandated transgender welfare board. No deviation from the national position material enough to score separately; assessed at the national score.

sources.summary: Human Rights Watch statement (26 March 2026) on India's 2026 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill passed by parliament: removes self-identification, limits legal recognition to hijra/kinner and intersex categories, mandates medical certification, and adds offences carrying up to life imprisonment for "coercing or alluring" someone to be transgender. The Goa dossier found no divergent Goa statute, so this national framework — not any local law — defines Goa's position for visitors.

BBC report (26 March 2026): both houses passed the amendment scrapping self-identification and requiring medical-board certification, amid protests; a Supreme Court-appointed panel sought withdrawal and presidential assent is pending. Applies nationally including Goa; no regional coverage, consistent with the dossier's finding of no Goan divergence in trans law or enforcement.

Times of India (Kolkata edition, 18 August 2024): alleged "gender check" groping of a transwoman by an RPF constable at Rabindra Sadan metro station, denied by authorities with a counter-FIR. A West Bengal incident, not about Goa, held as a national datapoint on police/security screening behaviour toward gender-nonconforming people in public spaces.
